title.en: Present the plan for a small business
title.es: Presentar el plan de un pequeño negocio

es: Presentar un plan de arranque para un negocio propio: calendario con plazos, tareas delegadas, un riesgo con su contingencia y respuesta a una objeción.

vocabulary.es: entender su argumento, darle la razón en eso

teaching.en: Thank you for coming; I will begin my pitch with the timeline, then turn to the forecast and the risks.
teaching.es: Gracias por venir; empezaré mi presentación con el calendario y después pasaré a la previsión y a los riesgos.
teaching.explanationEs: Una apertura clara anuncia el orden de la presentación.
segments: Thank you for coming; I will begin my pitch with
the timeline, then turn to the forecast and the risks.
teaching.audioText: Thank you for coming; I will begin my pitch with the timeline, then turn to the forecast and the risks.

teaching.en: We forecast fifty repairs a month by December, and we can back up that figure with two months of real orders.
teaching.es: Prevemos cincuenta reparaciones al mes para diciembre, y podemos respaldar esa cifra con dos meses de pedidos reales.
teaching.explanationEs: Forecast también es verbo; back up = apoyar una afirmación con datos.
segments: We forecast fifty repairs a month by December, and we can
back up that figure with two months of real orders.
teaching.audioText: We forecast fifty repairs a month by December, and we can back up that figure with two months of real orders.

teaching.en: An investor may raise an objection that cycling drops in winter, and a fair question deserves a direct answer.
teaching.es: Un inversor puede plantear la objeción de que el ciclismo baja en invierno, y una pregunta razonable merece una respuesta directa.
teaching.explanationEs: Raise an objection = plantear una objeción; fair question = pregunta legítima.
segments: An investor may raise an objection that cycling drops in
winter, and a fair question deserves a direct answer.
teaching.audioText: An investor may raise an objection that cycling drops in winter, and a fair question deserves a direct answer.

teaching.en: I take your point, but let me reassure you: we have a contingency plan for every major risk.
teaching.es: Entiendo su argumento, pero permítame tranquilizarle: tenemos un plan de contingencia para cada riesgo importante.
teaching.explanationEs: Take your point reconoce la objeción sin rendirse; reassure lleva a la persona como objeto directo.
segments: I take your point, but let me reassure you:
we have a contingency plan for every major risk.
teaching.audioText: I take your point, but let me reassure you: we have a contingency plan for every major risk.

teaching.en: I would like to address your objection briefly, because a realistic plan should stand by its figures.
teaching.es: Me gustaría responder brevemente a su objeción, porque un plan realista debe mantener sus cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Address = abordar una cuestión; stand by = mantener lo dicho cuando se cuestiona.
segments: I would like to address your objection briefly, because
a realistic plan should stand by its figures.
teaching.audioText: I would like to address your objection briefly, because a realistic plan should stand by its figures.

teaching.en: A calm answer backed by data can win over a doubtful investor far more effectively than a long speech.
teaching.es: Una respuesta serena respaldada por datos puede convencer a un inversor dudoso mucho mejor que un discurso largo.
teaching.explanationEs: Win over = ganarse el apoyo de alguien; la calma y los datos pesan más que la extensión.
segments: A calm answer backed by data can win over a
doubtful investor far more effectively than a long speech.
teaching.audioText: A calm answer backed by data can win over a doubtful investor far more effectively than a long speech.

prompt.es: Completa: «Permítame tranquilizarle: tenemos un plan para cada semana de lluvia.»

feedback.es: Reassure es transitivo: Let me reassure you, sin preposición.

origin.text: You said that the plan depends on good weather. Let me ___ you: we have a contingency plan for every wet week.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta reconoce la objeción y después responde con un dato?

choices.text: Your point is wrong, so please stop asking about the figure in winter.
I take your point, but two months of real orders already back up that figure.
I agree with your point, so the figure is probably too high and I will lower it.

feedback.es: Reconoce la objeción con I take your point y responde con un dato que respalda la cifra, sin rendirse ni atacar.

hint.es: Reconoce y después aporta un dato.

origin.text: Investor: Your forecast assumes fifty repairs a month, but winter is slow for cyclists. Why should I believe that number?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Permítanme empezar con el calendario y la previsión.»

answer.text: Let me begin with the timeline and the forecast

feedback.es: Let me + verbo base es una fórmula cortés de apertura.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta es la más adecuada ante la objeción del inversor?

choices.text: I take your point, so I will lower the forecast to thirty repairs and leave the rest of the plan.
I do not take your point, because competitors always exaggerate their own figures.
I take your point, but both competitors close on Sundays, and those are the customers we are aiming for.

feedback.es: La mejor respuesta reconoce el argumento y aporta un dato concreto; las otras ceden sin razón o descalifican sin pruebas.

origin.text: Investor: Your forecast of fifty repairs a month is not realistic. The two competitors near the station have been open for years, and neither reaches thirty.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la hablante ante la objeción.

choices.text: She answers the concern directly and offers the evidence if the listener wants it.
She dismisses the concern as unimportant because winter rarely affects demand.
She accepts the concern and offers to lower the forecast.

feedback.es: Responde a la preocupación y ofrece compartir las cifras: transparencia sin evasivas.

origin.audio: Thank you for that question. I would like to address it briefly. We have a contingency plan, so please let me reassure you: if the winter is slow, we will offer home repairs and draw on the cash reserve. I hope that answers your concern, and I am happy to share the figures.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nuestra previsión sigue siendo de cincuenta reparaciones al mes.»

feedback.es: Forecast es la previsión de resultados; target, estimate y projection son alternativas posibles en este contexto.

origin.text: We have planned for several scenarios. Even so, our ___ for the first year remains fifty repairs a month, which we consider realistic.

prompt.es: Presenta el plan: calendario, encargos, un riesgo y respuesta a la objeción.

answer.text: Thank you for coming. I will begin my pitch with the timeline. By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and we are getting the permit approved by the council. Meanwhile, Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter, and this time next month we will be putting up the shelves. By the first of June, we will have opened the doors. The main risk is a fall in demand in winter. Should demand fall, we will draw on our cash reserve and offer home repairs; failing that, we will shorten our opening hours. I take your point about the forecast, but let me reassure you: fifty repairs a month is realistic, because two competitors are already busy and there is a niche for fast repairs near the station. We can back up that figure with two months of real orders, and I would be glad to answer any other question.
accepted: Thank you for coming. I will begin my pitch with the timeline. By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and we are getting the permit approved by the council. Meanwhile, Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter, and this time next month we will be putting up the shelves. By the first of June, we will have opened the doors. The main risk is a fall in demand in winter. Should demand fall, we will draw on our cash reserve and offer home repairs; failing that, we will shorten our opening hours. I take your point about the forecast, but let me reassure you: fifty repairs a month is realistic, because two competitors are already busy and there is a niche for fast repairs near the station. We can back up that figure with two months of real orders, and I would be glad to answer any other question.

Good morning, and thank you for listening. First, the timeline: by the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and this week we are getting the permit approved by the council. Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter, and in a month we will be putting up the shelves. By June we will have opened the doors. The main risk is that demand may fall in winter. In the event of a fall in demand, we will use our cash reserve, and we will offer home repairs as well. I understand your objection, and let me reassure you: our forecast of fifty repairs a month is realistic, because there is a niche for fast repairs near the station. We can back up that figure with real orders, and I am happy to answer your questions.

Thank you all for being here. I will start with the calendar. By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and this week we are getting the permit approved by the council. Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter, and next month we will be painting the walls. By the first of June, we will have opened the doors. Our main risk is a slow winter. Should winter sales fall, we will draw on the reserve and offer home repairs; failing that, we will reduce our hours. I take your point about the forecast, but let me reassure you: fifty repairs a month is realistic, and we stand by that figure because two months of real orders back it up.

feedback.es: Una buena presentación tiene apertura, calendario con futuros, encargos, un riesgo con contingencia y una respuesta que reconoce y tranquiliza.

origin.text: Presentación ante un inversor. Incluye: apertura; calendario (contrato firmado a finales de marzo; estanterías dentro de un mes; apertura el 1 de junio); dos encargos (cartel y permiso); el riesgo de la demanda en invierno con su contingencia; y respuesta a la objeción «¿Es realista su previsión de cincuenta reparaciones al mes?». Escribe entre 120 y 200 palabras.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud expresa el inversor en su mensaje?

choices.text: Positive about the plan, but he will only back it if the owners lower their forecast.
Doubtful about the owners' honesty, although he admires the timeline.
Unsure about the idea itself, and wanting another investor's opinion first.
Interested but not ready to commit until the forecast is tested in a slow month.

feedback.es: No dice que no: pide ver un mes flojo antes de comprometer dinero, y valora la honestidad sobre el invierno.

origin.text: Thank you for the pitch. I liked the timeline and the honesty about winter. My hesitation is the forecast: it rests on two months of orders, both in summer. I am not saying no. I am saying that I would want to see one slow month before committing any money, and I would like the owners to tell me how they would respond if that month turned out badly. Please send me the monthly order figures from last winter, if you have them, and any letters from customers who have asked for home repairs. With that information, I believe we can have a useful second conversation, and I would gladly visit the workshop myself.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué propósito termina así su intervención el ponente.

choices.text: To concede the investor's point about winter and offer to cut the forecast.
To reassure the investor that nothing can go wrong with the forecast.
To invite the investor to check the figure instead of accepting it on trust.

feedback.es: Mantiene la cifra («I stand by the figure») y propone que el inversor la compruebe: confianza sin exigir fe ciega.

origin.audio: To sum up, I have shown you a timeline, two delegated tasks and one contingency plan. You asked whether the forecast is realistic. I take your point about winter, and I will not pretend that nothing can go wrong. But I stand by the figure, and I would rather you test it against the first three months than take my word for it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una pregunta razonable: nadie puede estar seguro del invierno.»

feedback.es: A fair question es una pregunta legítima, y abre una respuesta serena.

origin.text: That is a fair ___: nobody can be certain about winter, and the plan says so openly.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjeme responder primero a su objeción sobre el invierno.»

answer.text: Let me address your objection about winter first

feedback.es: Address your objection es la fórmula para responder de forma directa a una objeción.

choices.text: That is a fair question: it could happen, but our customer list and our good name would be hard to copy.
That will never happen, because nobody else in the city has ever thought of this idea.
It is a fair question, but the risk is so small that I prefer not to discuss it.

feedback.es: Reconoce el riesgo y ofrece un argumento realista; las otras respuestas prometen demasiado o ignoran la pregunta.

origin.text: Investor: What if another workshop copies your idea and opens next door?

prompt.es: Relaciona cada parte de la presentación con su función.

pairs: Let me begin with the timeline.
By June, we will have opened the doors.
Should demand fall, we will draw on our reserve.
I take your point, but let me reassure you.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: abrir, fijar un plazo, prever un riesgo y responder a la objeción.
